SYNTHETIC: This is a made-up deal for testing, matching the worked example in docs/background.md and the challenge brief. It is not a real project, building, city, program or buyer. Every number is a rounded ASSUMPTION based on a typical project. Do not cite it as a benchmark.
name: SYNTHETIC one-home bill (worked example)

time_costs_while_waiting.label: ASSUMPTION
time_costs_while_waiting.note: Lane 2 · Clear it. Loan interest, property taxes, insurance and management while the project waits. Invented.

family_price.label: ASSUMPTION
family_price.note: Fixed by income. A real tool would derive this from a dated income-limits table, the affordable-cost formula in the statute, a mortgage rate, taxes and insurance. Invented.

public_subsidies.label: ASSUMPTION
public_subsidies.note: Lane 3 · Fund it. Placeholder city and state funds, not real programs.

rent_earned_while_waiting.label: ASSUMPTION
rent_earned_while_waiting.note: Lane 3 · Fund it. Earned income from an existing building while it is held. Invented.

fundraising_the_gap.label: ASSUMPTION
fundraising_the_gap.note: Lane 3 · Fund it. Whatever is left after the other sources. Placeholder donors.

balance.label: ASSUMPTION (derived)
balance.note: The equation: what the family can pay + subsidies + fundraising (and earned income) − cost to create = $0.

time_sensitivity.label: ASSUMPTION
time_sensitivity.note: In the typical project this is based on, a 10-month schedule slip made the fundraising needed grow about 7 times. Time is money on both sides of the equation.
